title: Third Country Deportations Cuba
report:
**Summary:**
A Cuban immigrant, Arístides Fernandez-Garcia, was arrested by ICE and deported to the Central African Republic, a country he has no ties to, as part of the Trump administration's "third country deportation" policy. Fernandez-Garcia, who had been seeking asylum in the US, was not given a chance to express his fear of being sent to another country. He and his roommate, Yasmany Noel Moreno-De Armas, also a Cuban immigrant, claim they don't feel safe returning to Cuba due to persecution by the regime. The two men are now in limbo in the Central African Republic.

**Key Facts:**

1. Over 25,000 people have been deported to countries they have no ties to under the Trump administration's "third country deportation" policy.
2. A federal appeals court ruled on September 18 that this policy violates due process, as migrants are not given enough notice or a chance to express their fear of being sent to another country.
3. Arístides Fernandez-Garcia, a Cuban immigrant, was deported to the Central African Republic despite not having a deportation order and no record of criminal charges in Florida.
4. Fernandez-Garcia and his roommate, Yasmany Noel Moreno-De Armas, claim they were not given notice or assurances about their destination country before being deported.
5. The Trump administration has appealed the federal appeals court ruling to the Supreme Court, arguing that "third country removals" are essential for public safety.
